rows.guard: Do not promote a parcel boundary coordinate as survey-grade merely because it was digitised from a title-plan line.
Do not treat enlargement of mapping as an accuracy improvement; original survey specification remains controlling.
Do not infer a sub-metre parcel edge from line-centre scaling when the source mapping tolerance is larger.
Keep horizontal boundary uncertainty separate from vertical elevation uncertainty in any height-difference result.
Reject any workflow that equates general title-plan red edging with a surveyed legal boundary.
Require a boundary evidence class to be recorded before using boundary vertices for elevation sampling.
If only a general boundary is available, mark parcel-edge elevation as boundary-uncertain rather than exact.
Do not convert hedge, wall or fence depiction into legal-boundary certainty without corroborating evidence.
Require scale, orientation and datum provenance before treating a development survey as high-precision boundary evidence.
Reject PDF-derived scale measurements if print scaling is not verified.
Where survey and OS mapping materially differ, preserve the discrepancy instead of snapping one source to the other.
Promote survey-derived candidate geometry only when its stated tolerance is compatible with the requested elevation precision.
Require the metadata survey index for each sampled parcel so survey date/provenance is not lost.
Do not treat 1 m cell size as 1 m vertical accuracy; retain the stated ±15 cm RMSE separately.
Prefer the newest appropriate time-stamped survey when temporal mismatch could change terrain.
Record survey resolution and date per candidate; do not mix resolutions/dates without provenance.
Do not use OS Terrain 5 as a precision substitute for Environment Agency 1 m LIDAR when the latter is available.
Do not interpret 5 m post spacing as vertical accuracy.
Mark OS Terrain 5 derived parcel height differences as fallback-grade rather than official high-precision measurements.
Require interpolation method to be recorded when parcel sample points do not coincide with Terrain 5 posts.
Do not treat GNSS/WGS84 coordinates as OSGB36 National Grid coordinates without an explicit transformation.
Require vertical-datum provenance before comparing heights from separate sources.
Keep GNSS heighting error separate from OSGM15 model error in the uncertainty budget.
Do not use legacy triangulation agreement as parcel-boundary precision evidence.
